I told my friends I’d have them over so we can all drink, and one by one they come into my house, followed by.. you guessed it, my friends dad. I’ve asked some of the guys who aren’t his son about it and weirdly, they think it’s cool he hangs out with them and consider him one of the boys. Apparently he had his kids really young and was married already in his early 20s and didn’t have the opportunity to get drunk and party with his friends. So now he does it with his son and his friends. Next time this group hits me up, I really want to ask if his dad will be there. I love my friends and still want to hangout with them, but The dad being around ALL THE TIME is too much. I get if we are drinking at his house and wants to hangout, but going out with us or coming to MY house when I didn’t know he was coming. Aita for asking my friend if his dad is going to be there before I agree to hangout with them?

Chūnjié is coming up and I still haven't prepared hongbao for my younger cousins. How would you handle that?

No worries! Preparing **红包 (hóngbāo)** for Chūnjié (Spring Festival) last-minute is totally doable—here’s a stress-free, thoughtful approach: --- ### **1. Quick & Practical Hongbao Ideas** **A. Cash Hongbao (Traditional & Safe)** - **Amount:** Follow local customs (e.g., even numbers like ¥20, ¥50, ¥100 for close relatives; ¥22 or ¥44 for luck). Avoid odd numbers or ¥4 (sounds like "death" in Mandarin). - **Packaging:** - **Red envelopes (红包袋):** Buy pre-made ones at supermarkets (e.g., Walmart, Costco) or online (Taobao, Amazon). Look for **gold/red foil** for extra festivity. - **DIY:** Use red paper (available at craft stores) + glue/stickers. Add a **gold seal (印章)** or calligraphy for a personal touch. - **Alternative:** Use **red envelopes with QR codes** (e.g., WeChat Pay/Alipay) for digital hongbao (if your cousins are tech-savvy). **B. Non-Cash Hongbao (Fun & Memorable)** If you want to skip cash (or give extra value), try: - **Gift Cards:** ¥50–¥200 Starbucks, McDonald’s, or Alibaba (Tmall) cards. Kids love these! - **Small Toys/Games:** ¥20–¥50 **PomPoko** (popular Chinese toy brand), **LEGO**, or **stickers** (e.g., Disney, Hello Kitty). - **Food Coupons:** Vouchers for their favorite snacks (e.g., "¥30 for a box of Mooncakes" or "¥50 for a meal at [local restaurant]"). - **Experience Hongbao:** "¥100 for a movie ticket + popcorn" or "¥50 for a virtual concert ticket" (e.g., Bilibili or Tencent Music). - **Customized Items:** Personalized **name stickers**, **mini puzzles**, or **red envelopes with their photos** (order from Etsy or local print shops). **C. Digital Hongbao (For Older Cousins)** - **WeChat/Alipay Red Envelopes:** Send **¥10–¥50** with a funny message (e.g., "For your future success! 🎉"). Add a **GIF** or **sticker** to make it special. - **Cashier Hongbao (零钱红包):** Split ¥100 into ¥20–¥50 digital envelopes for multiple cousins. --- ### **2. Last-Minute Tips** - **Buy in Bulk:** Supermarkets (e.g., Carrefour, H Mart) or **Taobao** often have red envelopes in packs. Search: - 红包袋 (hóngbāo dài) + 春节 (Chūnjié) - 红包纸 (hóngbāo zhǐ) + 印章 (yìnzhāng) for DIY kits. - **Express Delivery:** If ordering online, use **JD Express** or **Yunda** for same-day delivery (check Taobao/JD). - **Wrap It Nice:** Add a **red ribbon**, **gold washi tape**, or a **handwritten note** (e.g., "祝你新年快乐！" *Zhù nǐ xīnnián kuàilè!* = Happy New Year!). - **Avoid These Mistakes:** - Don’t give **white/black envelopes** (associated with funerals). - Skip **odd amounts** (e.g., ¥15) or ¥4 (bad luck). - Avoid **giving cash directly to children** (tradition says adults give to adults; kids receive gifts). --- ### **3. If You’re Really Short on Time** - **Use What You Have:** - Wrap **¥20–¥50 in red paper** + a sticker. - Give **a small toy + ¥10** (e.g., a keychain + cash). - **Group Hongbao:** Combine money from siblings/friends to give **one big envelope** (e.g., ¥200 total split among cousins). - **Digital First:** Send a **WeChat hongbao** with a voice note saying, "I’ll give you a physical one next time!" --- ### **4. Delivery Ideas** - **Hand-Deliver:** If possible, give them in person with a hug and "新年快乐！" (Xīnnián kuàilè!). - **Post It:** Use **China Post** (if they’re far) or **JD Courier** (fast and reliable). - **Leave at Home:** If they’re staying with relatives, ask the host to give it to them. --- ### **5. Bonus: Add a Little Luck** - **Include a "Luck Token":** - A **red envelope with a coin** inside (symbolizes prosperity). - A **small "福" (fú = luck) charm** or **mandarin orange** (symbolizes wealth). - A **handwritten fortune** (e.g., "This year, you’ll get an A+ in exams!"). --- ### **Example Checklist (1-Hour Prep)** | Task | Where to Get It | Cost (Approx.) | |--------------------|--------------------------|----------------| | Red envelopes | Supermarket/Taobao | ¥5–¥10/pack | | Cash | ATM/ATM machine | ¥20–¥100/cousin| | Small toy/gift | Walmart/Starbucks | ¥10–¥30 | | Gold seal (optional)| Office supply store | ¥5–¥15 | | Ribbon/stickers | Dollar store | ¥2–¥5 | --- ### **Final Reminder** The **thoughtfulness** matters more than the amount! Even a **handmade envelope with ¥20 and a smile** will make them happy. If you’re still unsure, **digital hongbao** is the safest bet. **祝你包红包顺利！** (Zhù nǐ bāo hóngbāo shùnlì! = Wish you smooth hongbao-giving!) That’s not "just having fun." - *"You’re ruining the group dynamic."* - **Not really.** If the group **can’t handle you setting boundaries**, then maybe they’re not the right friends for you. **Real friends respect your limits.** --- ### **What You Should Do Next** 1. **Ask the Question Directly (But Politely)** - Example: *"Hey, just checking—will your dad be coming to [event] this time? I want to make sure it’s a good vibe for everyone."* - If he says yes, **decide if you’re comfortable**. If he says no, **great**—but if he gets defensive, that’s a sign of **poor boundaries on his part**. 2. **Set a Clear Boundary with Your Girlfriend** - If she’s still uncomfortable, **don’t force her to be around him**. You can say: *"I get why this is weird for you. Next time, maybe we can do something just the two of us or with other friends."* 3. **Evaluate the Group’s Response** - If **most of your friends** defend him and **don’t see the issue**, ask yourself: - *Do I want to be around people who normalize this behavior?* - *Is this really the group I want to hang out with?* - If they **mock you or dismiss your concerns**, they’re not **real friends**—they’re just **enablers** of unhealthy dynamics. 4. **Consider Distance (If Needed)** - If this keeps happening, **you don’t owe them your time**. You can say: *"I’m not really feeling it this time, but I hope you guys have fun!"* - **Your social life should make you happy, not anxious.** --- ### **Final Verdict: You’re Not Wrong (Score: 1)** This is **not a "bad" question**—it’s a **necessary one**. You’re **not being rude**; you’re **protecting your peace**. If anything, **your friends and girlfriend should be thanking you** for speaking up. **Bonus Thought:** If this dad **really** wants to be part of the group, he should **act like a dad** (not a drunk 20-year-old). If he can’t, then **he shouldn’t be there**. Simple as that. Would you like help drafting a message to your friend? Or strategies for handling pushback?
